text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The International Cricket Council is due to be completely revamped in an attempt to make the organisation more relevant and functional towards modern issues in the game. The council will be split into two, with former Test players taking a greater role with respect to rules, playing conditions and other technical matters. Page 18.

The A$150,000 still owing to Australia from the World Cup, currently being held as compensation for Australia's refusal to play their opening match in Sri Lanka following a bomb blast in the capital, may be returned as part of the latest moves towards peace in the cricket world. Page 18.

The perception that the popularity of the NBL has plateaued and is now in the process of waning has been confirmed by a recent drop in attendance figures. The average crowd for the 1996 season fell by seven percent to 68 percent of venue capacity. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Melbourne Cup winner Saintly is due to return to the hands of trainer Bart Cummings after release from quarantine tomorrow. Cummings, who has been unable to see the horse during the quarantine period, said reports are he is doing well. Page 3.
Australian Jason Stoltenberg beat world-ranked number four Goran Ivanisevic on September 22, ending the year as Australia's best-performed tennis player, and a Davis Cup hero. Page 43.

ARL Sydney City Roosters chairman Nick Politis yesterday confirmed the Roosters have received encouragement from Soccer Australia as they prepare a business plan to enter a team in the National Soccer League. Page 44.
THE AGE

After accepting support from the National Bank and becoming part of Team National, Daniel Kowalski, Lauren Hewitt and Emma George can no longer be members of the Victorian Institute of Sport, which is sponsored by the Commonwealth Bank. Page C8.

Tennis players Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge have signed contracts with entertainment impresario Michael Edgley, concerned that their income does not reflect their true achievements. Despite being world champions their only equipment and clothing deal is with Wilson, and their only non-tennis endorsement is for a brand of yoghurt. Page C8.

After a marathon VRC hearing, Victorian gallops trainer John Leek has been found guilty of administering a prohibited substance to his filly Lotilla before taking her to Flemington. VRC stewards handed down a two month suspension after elevated bicarbonate levels were found in the filly. Page C8.
THE HERALD SUN

Criticisms of the Olympic bonus awarded to tennis players the "Woodies" have been slammed by Australian Davis Cup captain John Newcombe. Newcombe asserted the "Woodies" - Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde - fully deserved their A$300,000 training bonus, and gave up a lot more money to represent Australia in Atlanta. Page 96.

Sydney's ultra-marathon runner Pat Farmer made a record-breaking time in his run across the Simpson Desert, declaring it his hardest run yet. Farmer broke the previously held record by 20 min 26 secs in a 379 km "sprint" from the Alka Selzter Bore. Page 96.
Cranbourne-based Victorian gallops trainer John Leek is the first to be suspended for an elevated bicarbonate reading. The suspension, passed down by VRC stewards, will last for two months. Page 98.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian women jockeys claim the most lucrative horse racing city in the country, Sydney, is also the most chauvinistic. Current licensing figures show just 11 of the 159 jockeys licensed in the Sydney metropolitan and provincial areas are women, and only two of these are Sydney-based. Page 54.

Sheffield Shield leaders Queensland will virtually cement home advantage for the season's cricket final should they beat the New South Wales Blues this week according to New South Wales cricket captain Greg Matthews. The Bulls will go into the match with a 10 point lead after outright wins in their three games. Page 56.

The New South Wales racing industry has called on the stater government to privatise the TAB and grant much needed taxation concessions in an effort to revive the wilting fortunes of the wagering market. It is argued racing industry leaders already own all TAB assets and should not have to pay for a significant holding in the off-course betting operation. Page 60.
